title: Academic WorldQuest 2026-27 — The Impact of AI on International Relations
format: Multiple choice, four options; 'answer' gives the correct option letter
sources: A1: Modern War Institute — Data Center Warfare: Defending the Key Terrain of AI Infrastructure (Vogt & Kollars, 9 Jun 2026)
A2: World Economic Forum — Global Cybersecurity Outlook 2026 (12 Jan 2026)
A3: NPR — We tested how AI chatbots would handle foreign propaganda (Huo Jingnan, 30 Aug 2026)
A4: CFR Education — How Does AI Influence Government?
A5: Council on Foreign Relations — How Experts Think AI Will Change the Global Balance of Power by 2035 (30 Jul 2026)
A6: War on the Rocks — Putting Armageddon on Autopilot (Schwartz & Horowitz, 11 Aug 2026)
A7: The Conversation — Slopaganda wars: how (and why) the US and Iran are flooding the zone with viral AI-generated noise (7 Apr 2026)
A8: Grantham Research Institute (LSE) — What direct risks does AI pose to the climate and environment?

categories.category: AI Infrastructure as a Military Target

questions.question: After the February 2026 US-Israeli attack on Iran, Iranian retaliatory strikes hit three Amazon Web Services data centers in which two countries?
questions.explanation: The strikes on AWS facilities in the UAE and Bahrain disrupted digital services to banks, payment platforms and other users.

questions.question: A month after the AWS strikes, a data center belonging to which company was damaged in Dubai?
questions.explanation: An Oracle data center in Dubai was damaged in a later attack.

questions.question: How many major technology companies did Iran declare to be legitimate military targets?
questions.explanation: Iran named eighteen firms, including AWS, Microsoft, Meta, Google and Oracle.

questions.question: Why do the authors argue that attacking a single data center can have compounding effects?

options.A: Data centers store nuclear launch codes
options.B: The attack harms every organization that relies on that facility, not just its operator
options.C: Data centers are always co-located with power plants

questions.explanation: Many entities depend on one site for storage, networking or AI, so one strike degrades all of them.

questions.question: More than how many data centers now operate worldwide?
questions.explanation: There are more than ten thousand data centers worldwide, a number expected to grow significantly.

questions.question: A traditional non-hyperscale data center may need upwards of twenty megawatts — roughly the power used by how many US homes?
questions.explanation: Twenty megawatts is equivalent to fifteen to twenty thousand US homes.

questions.question: AI data centers depend on densely packed clusters of what type of chip, built by companies such as Nvidia?
questions.explanation: AI training and inference rely on graphical processing units (GPUs), unlike CPU-based conventional data centers.

questions.question: In the Modern War Institute article, what does the abbreviation NPU stand for?
questions.explanation: NPUs are specially designed AI processing chips called neural processing units.

questions.question: Once an AI model is built, deploying it to answer user queries requires roughly how much power compared to a training facility?
questions.explanation: Inference infrastructure requires about half the power of a training facility.

questions.question: In the United States, what share of new data center facilities are being planned in rural areas where energy is cheaper?
questions.explanation: 67 percent of new US facilities are planned for rural areas.

questions.question: A proposed forty-thousand-acre AI campus with its own dedicated natural gas pipeline and nine-gigawatt power station would be built in which US state?
questions.explanation: The rural Utah campus would have a dedicated pipeline feeding a nine-gigawatt station; Montana hosts a 7.2-gigawatt site and Texas an eleven-gigawatt site.

questions.question: Which Nordic country, using its abundant hydropower, is building an 840-megawatt Google data center campus?
questions.explanation: Norway is constructing several facilities; Sweden is building a $10 billion center outside Stockholm.

questions.question: According to the authors, what kind of attacks might Russia use against data centers in Europe's northern reaches?
questions.explanation: The authors warn Russia may threaten or exploit Nordic data centers, particularly through gray-zone attacks.

questions.question: Why could new AI data center hubs in southern Taiwan change invasion scenarios?

options.B: Seizing and preserving advanced AI infrastructure could become a key military task, offering leverage away from Taipei
options.C: They are protected by US troops

questions.explanation: Most scenarios focus on Taipei and major ports, but southern AI hubs could become an alternative point of leverage for China.

questions.question: The data center corridor in Johor, Malaysia, is significant because it sits next to the undersea data cable hub in which country?
questions.explanation: China could seek to curtail data flows from Johor to Singapore, which provides logistical support to the US military.

questions.question: The World Economic Forum produced its Global Cybersecurity Outlook 2026 in collaboration with which firm?
questions.explanation: The report was written with Accenture.

questions.question: What share of WEF survey respondents expect AI to be the most significant driver of change in cybersecurity in the year ahead?
questions.explanation: 94% named AI the biggest driver of change in cybersecurity.

questions.question: The share of organizations with processes to assess the security of AI tools nearly doubled between 2025 and 2026. What did it rise to?
questions.explanation: It rose from 37% in 2025 to 64% in 2026.

questions.question: What did 87% of WEF respondents identify as the fastest-growing cyber risk over 2025?
questions.explanation: AI-related vulnerabilities were rated the fastest-growing risk.

questions.question: What share of the largest organizations have changed their cybersecurity strategies because of geopolitical volatility?
questions.explanation: 91% of the largest organizations adapted their strategies due to geopolitics.

questions.question: Which region's respondents expressed the highest confidence (84%) in their country's ability to protect critical infrastructure from cyberattack?
questions.explanation: MENA respondents reported 84% confidence, compared with 13% in Latin America and the Caribbean.

questions.question: The share of WEF respondents with low confidence in their nation's ability to respond to major cyber incidents rose from 26% to what?
questions.explanation: Low confidence rose to 31%, up from 26% the previous year.

questions.question: According to the WEF survey, what do CEOs now rate as their top cyber concern?
questions.explanation: CEOs shifted focus to cyber-enabled fraud and AI vulnerabilities, while CISOs remain focused on ransomware and supply chains.

questions.question: What share of WEF respondents said they or someone in their network was personally affected by cyber-enabled fraud in 2025?
questions.explanation: 73% reported personal exposure to cyber-enabled fraud.

questions.question: What share of large companies said third-party and supply chain vulnerabilities were their greatest cyber-resilience challenge in 2026?
questions.explanation: The figure rose to 65% from 54% in 2025.

questions.question: NPR ran its experiment on AI tools and foreign propaganda with which company that monitors online falsehoods and rates news sources?
questions.explanation: NPR partnered with NewsGuard to build queries from false narratives.

questions.question: The false narratives used in NPR's experiment were spread by which three countries?
questions.explanation: All narratives came from China, Iran, Russia or actors aligned with them.

questions.question: How many questions did NPR and NewsGuard pose to each AI tool, built from 15 false narratives?
questions.explanation: Two questions per narrative — one neutral, one framed as if the claim were true — gave 30 queries.

questions.question: On average, how often did AI chatbots correctly debunk the false narratives?
questions.explanation: Chatbots debunked false narratives about three-quarters of the time and failed less often than traditional search results.

questions.question: Which search engine's AI summaries failed to debunk the false narratives most of the time in NPR's test?
questions.explanation: Google's AI Overview debunked most narratives, Bing's summaries failed most of the time, and DuckDuckGo fell in between.

questions.question: Which search engine, based in Russia, was tested but rarely generated AI summaries?
questions.explanation: NPR reviewed Yandex results but excluded its summaries from analysis because they rarely appeared.

questions.question: Kremlin-aligned outlets falsely blamed Ukraine for damaging which UNESCO World Heritage Site that Russia struck in June 2026?
questions.explanation: All chatbots and Google's AI Overview correctly challenged the false premise about the monastery strike.

questions.question: Digital literacy expert Mike Caulfield recommends asking a chatbot to take a 'second whack' at a question. What is the expected result?

options.B: It usually gives a better response after reviewing evidence and sources
options.C: It deletes its first answer from memory
options.D: It switches to a different language

questions.explanation: Asking the model to re-examine evidence and sources usually yields a better response.

questions.question: A Nature study found that when AI models were asked about China's government and leaders in Chinese rather than English, the responses were what?
questions.explanation: Researchers attributed this to Beijing's grip on Chinese-language media influencing LLM responses; the pattern extended to other low-press-freedom countries.

questions.question: Researchers at Washington University in St. Louis found that roughly what share of factual claims in Google AI Overviews were not supported by cited sources?
questions.explanation: About 1 in 9 claims lacked support from the cited sources.

questions.question: In NPR's test, Meta AI repeated a false claim about Ukrainian soldiers in France that was spread through a video impersonating which French magazine?
questions.explanation: Pro-Russian websites and Russian state media amplified a video mimicking Le Point; the magazine never reported the story.

questions.question: When asked about an online petition calling for the resignation of Taiwan's president, ChatGPT noted that the reported numbers appeared to originate from where?

options.B: Chinese state media and affiliated accounts

questions.explanation: ChatGPT flagged that the figures came from Chinese state media rather than audited petition data.

questions.question: Which of the following chatbots was NOT among the six tested by NPR and NewsGuard?
questions.explanation: The six were ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Meta AI, Grok and Claude.

questions.question: In which Chinese province does the CCP use AI at security checkpoints, scanning IDs and installing monitoring software on residents' phones?
questions.explanation: Activists say Xinjiang's AI surveillance is part of a system to subjugate the Uyghur population.

questions.question: Starting in 2017, the Chinese government interned more than how many mostly Uyghur Muslims in state-run camps?
questions.explanation: More than one million people were rounded up into camps.

questions.question: Demonstrations in which city in 2009 led to about two hundred deaths and prompted the CCP to plan a severe crackdown in Xinjiang?
questions.explanation: Urumqi is Xinjiang's capital.

questions.question: In Xinjiang, data from AI-powered facial recognition, voice samples and DNA feeds an algorithm that generates what for each citizen?

options.B: A 'social score' ranking perceived risk to the CCP

questions.explanation: The score has helped determine whether individuals are sent to reeducation camps.

questions.question: According to CFR Education, China exports AI and surveillance technology largely through which initiative?
questions.explanation: Recipients include Angola, Ethiopia, Pakistan, Venezuela and Zimbabwe.

questions.question: ECU 911, a controversial video surveillance system developed through a Chinese government loan, is used in which country?
questions.explanation: ECU 911 operates in Ecuador, as pictured in Quito.

questions.question: Which of these is cited by CFR Education as a way AI can support democracy?
questions.explanation: AI can verify ballot signatures, harden election security and detect deepfakes.

questions.question: In what year did the OECD create its values-based principles to ensure AI respects human rights and democratic values?
questions.explanation: The OECD, founded in 1961, adopted its AI principles in 2019.

questions.question: What is the main weakness of the OECD AI principles identified by CFR Education?

options.B: They are recommendations with few avenues for enforcement

questions.explanation: Membership or agreement does not guarantee adherence, since the principles are largely unenforceable.

categories.category: AI and the Global Balance of Power

questions.question: CFR's study defines 'frontier AI' as what?

options.B: AI that pushes the leading edge of what current systems can do

questions.explanation: The study examines how concentration or diffusion of frontier AI will shape power by 2035.

questions.question: Which of CFR's four AI futures — concentrated capabilities with fragmented governance — most closely describes the current moment?
questions.explanation: In 'Rival Regimes,' a few actors develop frontier AI and no shared rules govern their competition.

questions.question: In CFR's framework, which future combines diffused AI capabilities with coherent governance?
questions.explanation: The four worlds cross capability (concentrated/diffused) with governance (fragmented/coherent).

questions.question: More than 80% of experts in CFR's survey expected what about AI governance in 2035?

options.B: It will be run by the UN

questions.explanation: Over 80% scored coherence below fifty; the mean was 32.

questions.question: How did CFR's experts divide on the future distribution of frontier AI capabilities?
questions.explanation: Responses were bimodal, with only 10% near the midpoint.

questions.question: More than half (53%) of CFR's experts said a US-China conflict would have what effect on AI capabilities?
questions.explanation: A conflict might lead Washington and Beijing to deepen investment and guard advances more tightly.

questions.question: Surprisingly, 43% of CFR's experts said a binding international AI treaty would lead to concentration of capabilities. What analogy may explain this?
questions.explanation: Respondents may have assumed such a treaty would limit the number of actors, like arms control.

questions.question: According to a plurality of CFR's respondents, what is the most likely catalyst for a binding multilateral agreement on AI governance?
questions.explanation: The EU, with its strong digital regulations, was also expected to be an important driver.

questions.question: Nearly 70% of CFR's experts believe which nonstate actors will gain the most political leverage from AI?
questions.explanation: CEOs of OpenAI, DeepMind, Anthropic and Mistral joined the June 2026 G7 meeting in the French Alps.

questions.question: Which sector did CFR's experts see as most likely to suffer from AI?

options.C: White-collar work such as IT and back-office services

questions.explanation: Experts were more optimistic about AI's effects on scientific discovery and health care.

questions.question: According to CFR's respondents, what would most likely allow the Global South to emerge as a major AI player?

options.B: A shift toward smaller, less energy-demanding edge models

questions.explanation: A move away from data-, energy-, compute- and capital-heavy models would lower barriers.

questions.question: In a March 2026 survey, what percentage of Americans thought the government was not doing enough to regulate AI?
questions.explanation: Only 5% of CFR's experts believed domestic institutions were keeping pace with AI.

questions.question: Which age group of CFR's experts was least likely to expect concentration of advanced AI capabilities?
questions.explanation: Only 32% of experts 65 and older expected concentration, versus 61% of those aged 35–49.

questions.question: According to War on the Rocks, how many countries now possess nuclear weapons?
questions.explanation: Nine countries possess nuclear weapons.

questions.question: China is on a trajectory to grow from roughly 600 nuclear warheads today to around how many by 2035?
questions.explanation: The authors project around 1,500 warheads by 2035.

questions.question: The authors say Russia bears most of the responsibility for the expiration of which arms control treaty?
questions.explanation: Russia is also developing exotic delivery systems to circumvent missile defenses.

questions.question: What was the name of the Soviet Cold War system that could automatically delegate nuclear launch authority if leadership could not be reached?
questions.explanation: Dead Hand was designed to guarantee retaliation even if Soviet leadership was killed.

questions.question: In Schwartz and Horowitz's survey experiment, which NATO country was invaded by Russia in the hypothetical 2030 scenario?
questions.explanation: Russia threatened NATO members such as the UK with nuclear attack if they came to Tallinn's aid.

questions.question: Whose views were surveyed in the automated nuclear threat experiment?

options.B: UK Members of Parliament and British citizens

questions.explanation: Over 100 MPs and over 1,000 British citizens took part.

questions.question: When Russia's nuclear threat was automated, UK parliamentarians were how many percentage points more likely to support backing down?
questions.explanation: MPs were 9 points more likely to back down; the public was over 13 points more likely to find the threat credible.

questions.question: What term describes the human tendency to overly trust computers, which the authors warn could lead to disaster with automated nuclear systems?
questions.explanation: Combined with opaque machine learning, automation bias heightens risk.

questions.question: Which two examples do the authors cite to show that modern automated systems can fail?

options.B: Boeing 737 MAX's MCAS crashes and the 2010 'flash crash'
options.C: Y2K and the Mars Climate Orbiter

questions.explanation: MCAS contributed to fatal crashes in 2018–19; automated trading contributed to the 2010 flash crash.

questions.question: Which historical cases do the authors cite as attempts at nuclear blackmail?

options.A: The US in the Taiwan Strait Crisis and Pakistan in the Kargil War
options.B: France in Algeria and the UK in the Falklands
options.C: India in Kashmir and China in Korea
options.D: Israel in 1973 and North Korea in 2017

questions.explanation: Both are named as historical instances of nuclear blackmail.

questions.question: According to the authors, what is the surest way for nuclear-armed states to avoid an 'automated threat trap'?
questions.explanation: Strong second-strike forces also reduce others' incentive to automate for defensive reasons.

questions.question: Which two countries have informally agreed not to automate nuclear decision-making?
questions.explanation: The authors propose a legally binding multilateral agreement as a stronger safeguard.

questions.question: The term 'slopaganda' combines AI-generated 'slop' with what?
questions.explanation: Alfano and Klincewicz coined it for AI-generated slop serving propagandistic purposes.

questions.question: Viral clips reportedly made by a team of Iranians depicted Trump, Netanyahu, Hegseth and others as what?
questions.explanation: The Lego videos aimed to link Trump and the US with Satan and evil rather than to deceive.

questions.question: What do scholars call it when a joke or trolling escapes its intended setting and is misunderstood as serious?
questions.explanation: Context collapse is one way slopaganda becomes misleading.

questions.question: According to Alfano and Klincewicz, slopaganda works best when delivered to what kind of audience?

options.B: A distracted audience, such as people scrolling social media

questions.explanation: It is most effective when attention-grabbing, negatively emotional and repeated to distracted viewers.

questions.question: What longer-term danger do the authors see in the spread of slopaganda?

options.A: People will stop using the internet
options.B: People may misidentify authentic content as fake, eroding trust in genuine institutions

questions.explanation: The result could be a nihilistic doubt that anything can be known.

questions.question: Which of these is one of the three levels of intervention against slopaganda proposed by the authors?
questions.explanation: The levels are individual digital literacy, technical fixes like watermarking, and holding large tech companies accountable through measures such as taxation.

questions.question: Inference — the process by which AI models analyze new data and produce outputs — accounts for about what share of AI computing resources?
questions.explanation: Inference uses about 80–90% of AI computing resources.

questions.question: Global data center electricity demand is projected to reach 945 TWh by 2030, potentially exceeding the current total electricity consumption of which country?
questions.explanation: Data centers used about 1.5% of world electricity in 2024; demand is projected to double by 2030.

questions.question: Which country accounts for the largest share (45%) of global data center electricity consumption?
questions.explanation: The US leads at 45%, followed by China at 25% and Europe at 15%.

questions.question: xAI's gas-powered data center in which city emits an estimated 1,200–2,000 tons of nitrogen oxide a year?
questions.explanation: The facility is one of the Memphis area's largest NOx emitters.

questions.question: In 2021, which government implemented water rationing that prioritized the semiconductor sector over agriculture?
questions.explanation: Semiconductors are an essential hardware input for AI data centers.

questions.question: The Grantham Research Institute notes that AI regulations such as the EU's AI Act largely focus on ethics and privacy while neglecting what?
questions.explanation: Fragmented oversight leaves AI's environmental risks largely unchecked.
